codes.heading: Early notification
codes.notes: Use for a complete record issued earlier than approximately six months before publication

codes.heading: Advance notification (confirmed)
codes.notes: Use for a complete record issued to confirm advance information approximately six months before publication; or for a complete record issued after that date and before information has been confirmed from the book-in-hand

codes.heading: Notification confirmed on publication
codes.notes: Use for a complete record issued to confirm advance information at or just before actual publication date, usually from the book-in-hand, or for a complete record issued at any later date

codes.heading: Update (partial)
codes.notes: In ONIX 3.0 or later only, use when sending a ‘block update’ record. A block update implies using the supplied block(s) to update the existing record for the product, replacing only the blocks included in the block update, and leaving other blocks unchanged – for example, replacing old information from Blocks 4 and 6 with the newly-received data while retaining information from Blocks 1–3, 5 and 7–8 untouched. In previous ONIX releases, and for ONIX 3.0 or later using other notification types, updating is by replacing the complete record with the newly-received data

codes.heading: Delete
codes.notes: Use when sending an instruction to delete a record which was previously issued. Note that a Delete instruction should NOT be used when a product is cancelled, put out of print, or otherwise withdrawn from sale: this should be handled as a change of Publishing status, leaving the receiver to decide whether to retain or delete the record. A Delete instruction is used ONLY when there is a particular reason to withdraw a record completely, eg because it was issued in error

codes.heading: Notice of sale
codes.notes: Notice of sale of a product, from one publisher to another: sent by the publisher disposing of the product

codes.heading: Notice of acquisition
codes.notes: Notice of acquisition of a product, by one publisher from another: sent by the acquiring publisher

codes.heading: Test update (partial)
codes.notes: Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later. Record may be processed for test purposes, but data should be discarded when testing is complete. Sender must ensure the <RecordReference> matches a previously-sent Test record

codes.heading: Test record
codes.notes: Record may be processed for test purposes, but data should be discarded when testing is complete. Sender must ensure the <RecordReference> does not match any previously-sent live product record

codes.heading: Single-component, not available separately
codes.notes: Used only when an ONIX record is required for a component-as-an-item, even though it is not currently available as such

codes.heading: Multiple-component retail product
codes.notes: Multiple-component product retailed as a whole

codes.heading: Multiple-item collection, retailed as separate parts
codes.notes: Used only when an ONIX record is required for a collection-as-a-whole, even though it is not currently retailed as such

codes.heading: Trade-only product
codes.notes: Product available to the book trade, but not for retail sale, and not carrying retail items, eg empty dumpbin, empty counterpack, promotional material

codes.heading: Multiple-item trade-only pack
codes.notes: Product available to the book trade, but not for general retail sale as a whole. It carries multiple components for retailing as separate items, eg shrink-wrapped trade pack, filled dumpbin, filled counterpack

codes.heading: Multiple-item pack
codes.notes: Carrying multiple components, primarily for retailing as separate items. The pack may be split and retailed as separate items OR retailed as a single item. Use instead of Multiple-item trade-only pack (code 30) if the data provider specifically wishes to make explicit that the pack may optionally be retailed as a whole

codes.heading: Proprietary product ID scheme
codes.notes: For example, a publisher’s or wholesaler’s product number or SKU. Note that a distinctive <IDTypeName> is required with proprietary identifiers

codes.heading: GTIN-13
codes.notes: GS1 Global Trade Item Number, formerly known as EAN article number (13 digits, without spaces or hyphens)

codes.heading: UPC
codes.notes: UPC product number (12 digits, without spaces or hyphens)

codes.heading: DOI
codes.notes: Digital Object Identifier (variable length and character set, beginning ‘10.’ and without https://doi.org/ or the older http://dx.doi.org/)

codes.heading: LCCN
codes.notes: Library of Congress Control Number in normalized form (up to 12 characters, alphanumeric)

codes.heading: GTIN-14
codes.notes: GS1 Global Trade Item Number (14 digits, without spaces or hyphens)

codes.heading: ISBN-13
codes.notes: International Standard Book Number, from 2007 (13 digits starting 978 or 9791–9799, without spaces or hyphens)

codes.heading: Legal deposit number
codes.notes: The number assigned to a publication as part of a national legal deposit process

codes.heading: URN
codes.notes: Uniform Resource Name: note that in trade applications an ISBN must be sent as a GTIN-13 and, where required, as an ISBN-13 – it should not be sent as a URN

codes.heading: OCLC number
codes.notes: A unique number assigned to a bibliographic item by OCLC

codes.heading: Co-publisher’s ISBN-13
codes.notes: An ISBN-13 assigned by a co-publisher. The ‘main’ ISBN sent with <ProductIDType> codes 03 and/or 15 should always be the ISBN that is used for ordering from the supplier identified in <SupplyDetail>. However, ISBN rules allow a co-published title to carry more than one ISBN. The co-publisher should be identified in an instance of the <Publisher> composite, with the applicable <PublishingRole> code

codes.heading: ISMN-13
codes.notes: International Standard Music Number, from 2008 (13-digit number starting 9790, without spaces or hyphens)

codes.heading: ISBN-A
codes.notes: Actionable ISBN, in fact a special DOI incorporating the ISBN-13 within the DOI syntax. Begins ‘10.978.’ or ‘10.979.’ and includes a / character between the registrant element (publisher prefix) and publication element of the ISBN, eg 10.978.000/1234567. Note the ISBN-A should always be accompanied by the ISBN itself, using <ProductIDType> codes 03 and/or 15

codes.heading: JP e-code
codes.notes: E-publication identifier controlled by JPOIID’s Committee for Research and Management of Electronic Publishing Codes. 20 alphanumeric characters, without spaces, beginning with the ISBN ‘registrant element’

codes.heading: OLCC number
codes.notes: Unique number assigned by the Chinese Online Library Cataloging Center (see http://olcc.nlc.gov.cn)

codes.heading: JP Magazine ID
codes.notes: Japanese magazine identifier, similar in scope to ISSN but identifying a specific issue of a serial publication. Five digits to identify the periodical, plus a hyphen and two digits to identify the issue

codes.heading: UPC-12+5
codes.notes: Used only with comic books and other products which use the UPC extension to identify individual issues or products. Do not use where the UPC-12 itself identifies the specific product, irrespective of any 5-digit extension – use code 04 instead

codes.heading: BNF Control number
codes.notes: Numéro de la notice bibliographique BNF

codes.heading: ISSN-13
codes.notes: International Standard Serial Number expressed as a GTIN-13, with optional 2- or 5-digit barcode extension (ie 13, 15 or 18 digits starting 977, without spaces or hyphens, with <BarcodeType> codes 02, 12 or 05), and only when the extended ISSN is used specifically as a product identifier (ie when the two publisher-defined ‘variant’ digits within the ISSN-13 itself and/or the 2- or 5-digit barcode extension are used to identify a single issue of a serial publication for separate sale). Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

codes.heading: ARK
codes.notes: Archival Resource Key, as a URL (including the address of the ARK resolver provided by eg a national library)

codes.heading: Digital file internal version number
codes.notes: Identifier for a specific revision of a particular product file or package of files, changed each time the file or package is modified in any way (eg to correct errors, update the content, or rebuild the package), whether the change is visible to the reader or not). For example, the ‘release identifier’ within an EPUB package such as ‘urn:uuid:a1b0d67e-2e81-4df5-9e67-a64cbe366809@2011-01-01T12:00:00Z’. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

codes.heading: Distinctive title (book); Cover title (serial); Title of content item, collection, or resource
codes.notes: The full text of the distinctive title of the item, without abbreviation or abridgement. For books, generally taken from the title page (see codes 11–15 where an alternative title is provided on cover or spine). Where the item is an omnibus edition containing two or more works by the same author, and there is no separate combined title, a distinctive title may be constructed (by the sender) by concatenating the individual titles, with suitable punctuation, as in ‘Pride and prejudice / Sense and sensibility / Northanger Abbey’. Where the title alone is not distinctive, recipients may add elements taken from a collection title and part number etc to create a distinctive title – but these elements should be provided separately by the sender

codes.heading: ISSN key title of serial
codes.notes: Serials only

codes.heading: Title in original language
codes.notes: Where the subject of the ONIX record is a translated item

codes.heading: Title acronym or initialism
codes.notes: For serials: an acronym or initialism of Title Type 01, eg ‘JAMA’, ‘JACM’

codes.heading: Abbreviated title
codes.notes: An abbreviated form of Title Type 01

codes.heading: Title in other language
codes.notes: A translation of Title Type 01 or 03, or an independent title, used when the work is translated into another language, sometimes termed a ‘parallel title’

codes.heading: Thematic title of journal issue
codes.notes: Serials only: when a journal issue is explicitly devoted to a specified topic

codes.heading: Former title
codes.notes: Books or serials: when an item was previously published under another title

codes.heading: Distributor’s title
codes.notes: For books: the title carried in a book distributor’s title file: frequently incomplete, and may include elements not properly part of the title. Usually limited in length and character set (eg to about 30 ASCII characters) for use on other e-commerce documentation

codes.heading: Alternative title on cover
codes.notes: An alternative title that appears on the cover of a book

codes.heading: Alternative title on back
codes.notes: An alternative title that appears on the back of a book

codes.heading: Expanded title
codes.notes: An expanded form of the title, eg the title of a school text book with grade and type and other details added to make the title meaningful, where otherwise it would comprise only the curriculum subject. This title type is required for submissions to the Spanish ISBN Agency

codes.heading: Alternative title
codes.notes: An alternative title that the book is widely known by, whether it appears on the book or not (including a title used in another market – but see code 06 for translations – or a working title previously used in metadata but replaced before publication)

codes.heading: Alternative title on spine
codes.notes: An alternative title that appears on the spine of a book. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

codes.heading: Translated from title
codes.notes: Where the subject of the ONIX record is a translated item, but has been translated via some intermediate language. Title type 16 is distinct from title type 03. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

codes.heading: By (author)
codes.notes: Author of a textual work

codes.heading: With
codes.notes: With or as told to: ‘ghost’ or secondary author of a literary work (for clarity, should not be used for true ‘ghost’ authors who are not credited on the book and whose existence is secret)

codes.heading: Screenplay by
codes.notes: Writer of screenplay or script (film or video)

codes.heading: Libretto by
codes.notes: Writer of libretto (opera): see also A31

codes.heading: Lyrics by
codes.notes: Author of lyrics (song): see also A31

codes.heading: By (composer)
codes.notes: Composer of music

codes.heading: By (artist)
codes.notes: Visual artist when named as the primary creator of, eg, a book of reproductions of artworks

codes.heading: By (photographer)
codes.notes: Photographer when named as the primary creator of, eg, a book of photographs

codes.heading: Created by
codes.notes: For example of an editorial concept, of a board game, etc

codes.heading: From an idea by
codes.notes: For example of a plot idea. Implies a less direct association or active participation than ‘created by’

codes.heading: Designed by
codes.notes: Use for interior graphic design. See code A36 for cover design, code A12, A35 for interior illustrations or drawings

codes.heading: Illustrated by
codes.notes: Artist when named as the creator of artwork which illustrates a text, or the originator (sometimes ‘penciller’ for collaborative art) of the artwork of a graphic novel or comic book

codes.heading: Photographs by
codes.notes: Photographer when named as the creator of photographs which illustrate a text

codes.heading: Text by
codes.notes: Author of text which accompanies art reproductions or photographs, or which is part of a graphic novel or comic book

codes.heading: Preface by
codes.notes: Author of preface

codes.heading: Prologue by
codes.notes: Author of prologue

codes.heading: Summary by
codes.notes: Author of summary

codes.heading: Supplement by
codes.notes: Author of supplement

codes.heading: Afterword by
codes.notes: Author of afterword

codes.heading: Notes by
codes.notes: Author of notes or annotations: see also A29

codes.heading: Commentaries by
codes.notes: Author of commentaries on the main text

codes.heading: Epilogue by
codes.notes: Author of epilogue

codes.heading: Foreword by
codes.notes: Author of foreword

codes.heading: Introduction by
codes.notes: Author of introduction: see also A29

codes.heading: Footnotes by
codes.notes: Author / compiler of footnotes

codes.heading: Memoir by
codes.notes: Author of memoir accompanying main text

codes.heading: Experiments by
codes.notes: Person who carried out experiments reported in the text

codes.heading: Interpreted through
codes.notes: Use with narratives drawn from an oral tradition, where no ‘ownership’ of the narrative is claimed. See also B33. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

codes.heading: Introduction and notes by
codes.notes: Author of introduction and notes: see also A20 and A24

codes.heading: Software written by
codes.notes: Writer of computer programs ancillary to the text

codes.heading: Book and lyrics by
codes.notes: Author of the textual content of a musical drama: see also A04 and A05

codes.heading: Contributions by
codes.notes: Author of additional contributions to the text

codes.heading: Appendix by
codes.notes: Author of appendix

codes.heading: Index by
codes.notes: Compiler of index

codes.heading: Cover design or artwork by
codes.notes: Use also for the cover artist of a graphic novel or comic book if named separately. Prefer code A56 to credit a graphic designer separately from the creator of the cover artwork

codes.heading: Preliminary work by
codes.notes: Responsible for preliminary work on which the work is based

codes.heading: Original author
codes.notes: Author of the first edition (usually of a standard work) who is not an author of the current edition

codes.heading: Maps by
codes.notes: Maps drawn or otherwise contributed by

codes.heading: Inked or colored by
codes.notes: Use for secondary creators when separate persons are named as having respectively drawn and inked / colored / finished artwork, eg for a graphic novel or comic book. Use with A12 for ‘drawn by’. Use A40 for ‘finished by’, but prefer more specific codes A46 to A48 instead of A40 unless the more specific secondary roles are inappropriate, unclear or unavailable

codes.heading: Paper engineering by
codes.notes: Designer or paper engineer of die-cuts, press-outs or of pop-ups in a pop-up book, who may be different from the illustrator

codes.heading: Continued by
codes.notes: Use where a standard work is being continued by somebody other than the original author

codes.heading: Comic script by
codes.notes: Writer of dialogue, captions in a comic book (following an outline by the primary writer)

codes.heading: Inker
codes.notes: Renders final comic book line art based on work of the illustrator or penciller (code A12). Preferred to code A40

codes.heading: Colorist
codes.notes: Provides comic book color art and effects. Preferred to code A40

codes.heading: Letterer
codes.notes: Creates comic book text balloons and other text elements (where this is a distinct role from script writer and/or illustrator), or creates calligraphy in non-comic products

codes.heading: Cover inker
codes.notes: Renders final comic book cover line art based on work of the cover designer (code A36), where different from the inker of the interior line art. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

codes.heading: Cover colorist
codes.notes: Provides comic book cover color art and effects, where different from the colorist of the interior art and effects. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

codes.heading: Research by
codes.notes: Person or organization responsible for performing research on which the work is based. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

codes.heading: Original character design
codes.notes: (for comic books). Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

codes.heading: Cover graphic design by
codes.notes: Use where the overall graphic designer of the cover is credited separately from the creator of the cover artwork. Use code A36 for the creator of the cover artwork (who could be a photographer, illustrator etc), or where only a single cover creator is credited. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

codes.heading: Other primary creator
codes.notes: Other type of primary creator not specified above

codes.heading: Adapted by
codes.notes: See also B22 (Dramatized by)

codes.heading: Translated with commentary by
codes.notes: This code applies where a translator has provided a commentary on issues relating to the translation. If the translator has also provided a commentary on the work itself, codes B06 and A21 should be used

codes.heading: Series edited by
codes.notes: Name of a series editor when the product belongs to a series

codes.heading: Founded by
codes.notes: Usually the founder editor of a serial publication (de: Begruendet von)

codes.heading: Consultant editor
codes.notes: Use also for ‘advisory editor’, ‘series advisor’, ‘editorial consultant’ etc

codes.heading: Dramatized by
codes.notes: See also B05 (Adapted by)

codes.heading: General rapporteur
codes.notes: In Europe, an expert editor who takes responsibility for the legal content of a collaborative law volume

codes.heading: Literary editor
codes.notes: Editor who is responsible for establishing the text used in an edition of a literary work, where this is recognized as a distinctive role (es: editor literario)

codes.heading: Technical editor
codes.notes: Responsible for the technical accuracy and language, may also be involved in coordinating and preparing technical material for publication

codes.heading: Scientific editor
codes.notes: Responsible overall for the scientific content of the publication

codes.heading: Historical advisor
codes.notes: Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

codes.heading: Original editor
codes.notes: Editor of the first edition (usually of a standard work) who is not an editor of the current edition. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

codes.heading: Translation revised by
codes.notes: Where possible, use with B06 for the original translator. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

codes.heading: Transcribed by
codes.notes: As told to. Use with narratives drawn from an oral tradition, and with B03 (Retold by), B07 (As told by) or A28 (Interpreted through). Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

codes.heading: Sensitivity reader / editor
codes.notes: Reader or editor responsible for ensuring the text is free of offensive, potentially offensive or insensitive language, is inclusive and free from bias, and avoids stereotypical characterization. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

codes.heading: Image descriptions by
codes.notes: Creator of alternative image descriptions for accessibility purposes. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

codes.heading: Text modernized or updated by
codes.notes: Use for modernization or minor updating of language, but not for original contributions to the text. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

codes.heading: Other adaptation by
codes.notes: Other type of adaptation or editing not specified above

codes.heading: Compiled by
codes.notes: For puzzles, directories, statistics, etc

codes.heading: Selected by
codes.notes: For textual material (eg for an anthology)

codes.heading: Non-text material selected by
codes.notes: Eg for a collection of photographs etc

codes.heading: Curated by
codes.notes: Eg for an exhibition

codes.heading: Other compilation by
codes.notes: Other type of compilation not specified above

codes.heading: Producer
codes.notes: Of a film, of a theatrical or multimedia production, of dramatized audio etc

codes.heading: Director
codes.notes: Of a film, of a theatrical or multimedia production, of dramatized audio etc

codes.heading: Conductor
codes.notes: Conductor of a musical performance

codes.heading: Choreographer
codes.notes: Of a dance performance. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

codes.heading: Other direction by
codes.notes: Other type of direction not specified above

codes.heading: Actor
codes.notes: Performer in a dramatized production (including a voice actor in an audio production)

codes.heading: Narrator
codes.notes: Where the narrator is a character in a dramatized production (including a voice actor in an audio production). For the ‘narrator’ of a non-dramatized audiobook, use code E07

codes.heading: Vocal soloist
codes.notes: Singer etc

codes.heading: Read by
codes.notes: Reader of recorded text, as in an audiobook

codes.heading: Performed by (orchestra, band, ensemble)
codes.notes: Name of a musical group in a performing role

codes.heading: Speaker
codes.notes: Of a speech, lecture etc

codes.heading: Presenter
codes.notes: Introduces and links other contributors and material, eg within a documentary

codes.heading: Introduction read by
codes.notes: Reader of recorded introduction (or other ‘front matter’) in an audiobook. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

codes.heading: Performed by
codes.notes: Other type of performer not specified above: use for a recorded performance which does not fit a category above, eg a performance by a stand-up comedian

codes.heading: Filmed / photographed by
codes.notes: Cinematographer, etc

codes.heading: Other recording by
codes.notes: Other type of recording not specified above

codes.heading: Assisted by
codes.notes: Contributor must follow another contributor with any contributor role, and placement should therefore be controlled by contributor sequence numbering to ensure the correct association

codes.heading: Enacting jurisdiction
codes.notes: For publication of laws, regulations, rulings etc. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

codes.heading: Peer reviewed
codes.notes: Use with <UnnamedPersons> code 02 as a ‘flag’ to indicate the publication is anonymously peer-reviewed. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

codes.heading: Posthumously completed by
codes.notes: Contributor must follow another (posthumous) contributor with any contributor role, and placement should therefore be controlled by contributor sequence numbering to ensure the correct association. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

codes.heading: In association with
codes.notes: Contributor must follow another contributor with any contributor role, and placement should therefore be controlled by contributor sequence numbering to ensure the correct association. See also ‘published in association with’ in List 45. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

codes.heading: (Various roles)
codes.notes: For use ONLY with ‘et al’ or ‘Various’ within <UnnamedPersons>, where the roles of the multiple contributors vary

codes.heading: Other
codes.notes: Other creative responsibility not falling within A to F above

codes.heading: Abridged edition
codes.notes: Content has been shortened: use for abridged, shortened, concise, condensed

codes.heading: Acting edition
codes.notes: Version of a play or script intended for use of those directly involved in a production, usually including full stage directions in addition to the text of the script

codes.heading: Adapted edition
codes.notes: Content has been adapted to serve a different purpose or audience, or from one medium to another: use for dramatization, novelization etc. Use <EditionStatement> to describe the exact nature of the adaptation

codes.heading: Annotated edition
codes.notes: Content is augmented by the addition of notes

codes.heading: Anniversary edition
codes.notes: Edition published to mark a special anniversary of first publication of the content. Use <EditionStatement> to describe the nature of the anniversary. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

codes.heading: Bilingual edition
codes.notes: Both languages should be specified in the <Language> group. Use MLL for an edition in more than two languages

codes.heading: Bilingual ‘facing page’ edition
codes.notes: Use only where the two languages are presented in parallel on facing pages, or in parallel columns of text on a single page (otherwise use BLL). Both languages should be specified in the <Language> group

codes.heading: Braille edition
codes.notes: Braille edition

codes.heading: Budget edition
codes.notes: Product sold at lower price than other editions, usually with lower quality paper or binding to reduce production costs. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

codes.heading: Combined volume
codes.notes: An edition in which two or more works also published separately are combined in a single volume; AKA ‘omnibus edition’ or occasionally ‘bind-up’, or in comic books a ‘trade paperback’ (fr: ‘intégrale’)

codes.heading: Critical edition
codes.notes: Content includes critical commentary on the text

codes.heading: Coursepack
codes.notes: Content was compiled for a specified educational course

codes.heading: Digital original
codes.notes: A digital product that, at the time of publication, has or had no physical counterpart and that is or was not expected to have a physical counterpart for a reasonable time (recommended at least 30 days following publication)

codes.heading: Enhanced edition
codes.notes: Use for e-publications that have been enhanced with additional text, speech, other audio, video, interactive or other content

codes.heading: Enlarged edition
codes.notes: Content has been enlarged or expanded from that of a previous edition, with significant additions to the original content – for example additional chapters. Do not use where the only additions are not a part of the original work (eg ‘teaser chapters’ from another work)

codes.heading: Easy-to-read edition
codes.notes: Book which uses highly simplified wording, clear page layout and typography to ensure the content can be understood by those with intellectual disabilities. See https://www.inclusion-europe.eu/easy-to-read for guidelines. See also SMP for editions with simplified language. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

codes.heading: Expurgated edition
codes.notes: ‘Offensive’ content has been removed

codes.heading: Facsimile edition
codes.notes: Exact reproduction of the content and format of a previous edition

codes.heading: Festschrift
codes.notes: A collection of writings published in honor of a person, an institution or a society

codes.heading: High readability edition
codes.notes: Edition optimized for high readability, typically featuring colored or tinted page backgrounds to reduce contrast, extra letter, word and line spacing to reduce crowding and isolate individual words, simplified page layouts and an open, sans serif font (or occasionally, an unusual font design) intended to aid readability. Sometimes labelled ‘dyslexia-friendly’. See also code SMP if the text itself is simplified, and codes LTE or ULP if the type size is significantly larger than normal. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

codes.heading: Illustrated edition
codes.notes: Content includes extensive illustrations which are not part of other editions

codes.heading: International edition
codes.notes: A product aimed specifically at markets other than the country of original publication, usually titled as an ‘International edition’ and with specification and/or content changes

codes.heading: Large type / large print edition
codes.notes: Large print edition, print sizes 14 to 19pt – see also ULP

codes.heading: Microprint edition
codes.notes: A printed edition in a type size too small to be read without a magnifying glass

codes.heading: Media tie-in
codes.notes: An edition published to coincide with the release of a film, TV program, or electronic game based on the same work. Use <EditionStatement> to describe the exact nature of the tie-in

codes.heading: Multilingual edition
codes.notes: All languages should be specified in the ‘Language’ group. Use BLL for a bilingual edition

codes.heading: New edition
codes.notes: Where no other information is given, or no other coded type or edition numbering is applicable

codes.heading: Edition with numbered copies
codes.notes: A limited or collectors’ edition in which each copy is individually numbered, and the actual number of copies is strictly limited. Note that the supplier may limit the number of orders fulfilled per retail outlet. Use <EditionStatement> to give details of the number of copies printed

codes.heading: Paperback original
codes.notes: A product published in any form of soft cover, that at the time of publication, has or had no counterpart in any other format, and that is or was not expected to have such a counterpart for a reasonable time (recommended at least 30 days following publication). Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

codes.heading: Prebound edition
codes.notes: Book that was previously bound, normally as a paperback, and has been rebound with, for example, a library-quality hardcover binding, or a lay-flat binding, by a supplier other than the original publisher. See also the <Publisher> and <RelatedProduct> composites for other aspects of the treatment of prebound editions in ONIX

codes.heading: Revised edition
codes.notes: Content has been revised from that of a previous edition (often used when there has been no corresponding increment in the edition number, or no edition numbering is available)

codes.heading: School edition
codes.notes: An edition intended specifically for use in schools

codes.heading: Signed edition
codes.notes: Individually autographed by the author(s)

codes.heading: Simplified language edition
codes.notes: An edition that uses simplified language, usually for second or additional language learners. See ETR for highly simplified editions for readers with intellectual disabilities

codes.heading: Special edition
codes.notes: Use for anniversary, collectors’, de luxe, gift, limited, signed, commemorative or celebratory, tie-in, special variant cover or otherwise special editions, but prefer more specific codes AVS, FST, MDT, NUM, SIG, UNN whenever appropriate. Use <EditionStatement> to describe the exact nature of the special edition

codes.heading: Student edition
codes.notes: Where a text is available in both student and teacher’s editions

codes.heading: Teacher’s edition
codes.notes: Where a text is available in both student and teacher’s editions; use also for instructor’s or leader’s editions, and for editions intended exclusively for educators where no specific student edition is available

codes.heading: Unabridged edition
codes.notes: Where a title has also been published in an abridged edition; also for audiobooks, regardless of whether an abridged audio version also exists

codes.heading: Ultra large print edition
codes.notes: For print sizes 20pt and above, and with typefaces designed for the visually impaired – see also LTE

codes.heading: Edition with unnumbered copies
codes.notes: A limited or collectors’ edition in which each copy is not individually numbered – but where the actual number of copies is strictly limited. Note that the supplier may limit the number of orders fulfilled per retail outlet. Use <EditionStatement> to give details of the number of copies printed

codes.heading: Unexpurgated edition
codes.notes: Content previously considered ‘offensive’ has been restored

codes.heading: Variorum edition
codes.notes: Content includes notes by various commentators, and/or includes and compares several variant texts of the same work

codes.heading: Readaloud edition
codes.notes: (de: Vorlesebücher) Edition specifically intended and designed for reading aloud (to children). Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

codes.heading: Original language of a translated text
codes.notes: Where the text in the original language is NOT part of the current product

codes.heading: Language of abstracts
codes.notes: Where different from language of text: used mainly for serials

codes.heading: Original language in a multilingual edition
codes.notes: Where the text in the original language is part of a bilingual or multilingual product

codes.heading: Translated language in a multilingual edition
codes.notes: Where the text in a translated language is part of a bilingual or multilingual product

codes.heading: Language of audio track
codes.notes: For example, on an audiobook or video product. Use for the only available audio track, or where there are multiple tracks (eg on a DVD), for an alternate language audio track that is NOT the original. (In the latter case, use code 11 for the original language audio if it is included in the product, or code 10 to identify an original language that is not present in the product)

codes.heading: Language of subtitles
codes.notes: For example, on a DVD or digital video with closed or open captions / subtitles

codes.heading: Language of original audio track
codes.notes: Where the audio in the original language is NOT part of the current product

codes.heading: Original language audio track in a multilingual product
codes.notes: Where the audio in the original language is part of a multilingual product with multiple audio tracks

codes.heading: Language of notes
codes.notes: Use for the language of footnotes, endnotes, annotations or commentary, instructions or guidance for use etc, where it is different from the language of the main text

codes.heading: Language of introduction / end matter
codes.notes: Use for the language of any introductory text, prologue, etc, or epilogue, end matter, etc, where it is different from the language of the main text. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

codes.heading: Target language of teaching / learning
codes.notes: Eg for the book ‘Ingles para latinos’, English. For phrasebooks and language teaching, learning or study material. Wherever possible, the language should also be listed as the subject of the book. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

codes.heading: Additional vocabulary / text in this language
codes.notes: Use of significant words, phrases, quotations or short passages from a language other than the main language of the text, as an integral part of the text. This does not include ‘loanwords’, academic Latin, etc. Only for use in ONIX 3.0 or later

codes.heading: Dewey
codes.notes: Dewey Decimal Classification

codes.heading: LC classification
codes.notes: US Library of Congress classification

codes.heading: LC subject heading
codes.notes: US Library of Congress subject heading

codes.heading: NLM classification
codes.notes: US National Library of Medicine medical classification

codes.heading: MeSH heading
codes.notes: US National Library of Medicine Medical subject heading

codes.heading: NAL subject heading
codes.notes: US National Agricultural Library subject heading

codes.heading: AAT
codes.notes: Getty Art and Architecture Thesaurus heading

codes.heading: UDC
codes.notes: Universal Decimal Classification

codes.heading: BISAC Subject Heading
codes.notes: BISAC Subject Headings are used in the North American market to categorize books based on topical content. They serve as a guideline for shelving books in physical stores and browsing books in online stores. See https://www.bisg.org/complete-bisac-subject-headings-list

codes.heading: BISAC Regional theme
codes.notes: A geographical qualifier used with a BISAC subject category

codes.heading: DDC-Sachgruppen der Deutschen Nationalbibliografie
codes.notes: Used for German National Bibliography since 2004 (100 subjects). Is different from value 30. See https://www.dnb.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/DE/Professionell/Erschliessen/ddcSachgruppenDNBAb2013.html (in German)

codes.heading: Keywords
codes.notes: For indexing and search purposes, not normally intended for display. Where multiple keywords or keyword phrases are sent, this should be in a single instance of the <SubjectHeadingText> element, and it is recommended that they should be separated by semi-colons (this is consistent with Library of Congress preferred practice)

codes.heading: BIC children’s book marketing category
codes.notes: See PA/BIC CBMC guidelines at https://bic.org.uk/resources/childrens-books-marketing-classifications/

codes.heading: BISAC Merchandising Theme
codes.notes: BISAC Merchandising Themes are used in addition to BISAC Subject Headings to denote an audience to which a work may be of particular appeal, a time of year or event for which a work may be especially appropriate, or to further describe fictional works that have been subject-coded by genre

codes.heading: Publisher’s own category code
codes.notes: Which is not in itself a subject scheme, but describes other attributes of the content, as specified in <SubjectSchemeName>

codes.heading: Proprietary subject scheme
codes.notes: For example, a publisher’s or retailer’s own subject coding scheme. Note that a distinctive <SubjectSchemeName> is required with proprietary coding schemes

codes.heading: Tabla de materias ISBN
codes.notes: Latin America

codes.heading: Warengruppen-Systematik des deutschen Buchhandels
codes.notes: See https://vlb.de/assets/images/wgsneuversion2_0.pdf (in German)

codes.heading: Thèmes Electre
codes.notes: Subject classification used by Electre (France)

codes.heading: CLIL Classification thématique
codes.notes: France. A four-digit number, see https://clil.centprod.com/listeActive.html (in French)

codes.heading: DNB-Sachgruppen
codes.notes: Deutsche Bibliothek subject groups. Used for German National Bibliography until 2003 (65 subjects). Is different from value 18. See http://www.dnb.de/service/pdf/ddc_wv_alt_neu.pdf (in German)

codes.heading: NUGI
codes.notes: Nederlandse Uniforme Genre-Indeling (former Dutch book trade classification)

codes.heading: NUR
codes.notes: Nederlandstalige Uniforme Rubrieksindeling (Dutch book trade classification, from 2002), see http://www.boek.nl/nur (in Dutch)

codes.heading: SISO
codes.notes: Schema Indeling Systematische Catalogus Openbare Bibliotheken (Dutch library classification)

codes.heading: Korean Decimal Classification (KDC)
codes.notes: A modified Dewey Decimal Classification used in the Republic of Korea

codes.heading: DDC Deutsch 22
codes.notes: German Translation of Dewey Decimal Classification 22. Also known as DDC 22 ger. See http://www.ddc-deutsch.de/produkte/uebersichten/

codes.heading: Bokgrupper
codes.notes: Norwegian book trade product categories (Bokgrupper) administered by the Norwegian Publishers Association (http://www.forleggerforeningen.no/)

codes.heading: Varegrupper
codes.notes: Norwegian bookselling subject categories (Bokhandelens varegrupper) administered by the Norwegian Booksellers Association (http://bokhandlerforeningen.no/)

codes.heading: Nippon Decimal Classification
codes.notes: Japanese subject classification scheme

codes.heading: BSQ
codes.notes: BookSelling Qualifier: Russian book trade classification

codes.heading: ANELE Materias
codes.notes: Spain: subject coding scheme of the Asociación Nacional de Editores de Libros y Material de Enseñanza

codes.heading: GREP Utdanningsprogram
codes.notes: Codes for Norwegian Educational program (‘utdanningsprogram’) used in secondary education. See https://www.udir.no/ and https://data.udir.no/kl06/v201906/utdanningsprogram

codes.heading: GREP Programområde
codes.notes: Codes for Norwegian educational Program area (‘programområde’) used in secondary education. See https://www.udir.no/ and https://data.udir.no/kl06/v201906/programomraader

codes.heading: Undervisningsmateriell
codes.notes: Bokbasen list of categories for books and other types of learning material used in education (‘undervisning’)

codes.heading: Norsk DDK
codes.notes: Norwegian version of Dewey Decimal Classification

codes.heading: Varugrupper
codes.notes: Swedish bookselling subject categories
