For binders intended for loose leaf or partwork publications intended to be updateable, see codes BD, BN

codes.heading: Plate (lámina)
codes.notes: A book-sized (as opposed to poster-sized) sheet, usually in color or high quality print

codes.heading: Notebook / blank book
codes.notes: A book with all pages blank for the buyer’s own use; may use <ProductFormDetail> codes P201 to P204 to specify binding

codes.heading: Organizer
codes.notes: May use <ProductFormDetail> codes P201 to P204 to specify binding

codes.heading: Leaflet
codes.notes: Folded but unbound

codes.heading: Book plates
codes.notes: Ex libris’ book labels and packs

codes.heading: Other printed item
codes.notes: Other printed item not specified by PB to PQ. Further detail is expected in <ProductFormDescription>, as <ProductFormDetail> and <ProductFormFeature> are unlikely to be sufficient

codes.heading: Multiple-component retail product
codes.notes: Presentation unspecified: format of product components must be given in <ProductPart>. Use only when the packaging of the product is unknown, or when no other S* code applies and the presentation is described in <ProductFormDescription>

codes.heading: Multiple-component retail product, boxed
codes.notes: Format of product components must be given in <ProductPart>

codes.heading: Multiple-component retail product, slip-cased
codes.notes: Format of product components must be given in <ProductPart>

codes.heading: Multiple-component retail product, shrink-wrapped
codes.notes: Format of product components must be given in <ProductPart>. Use code XL for a shrink-wrapped pack for trade supply, where the retail items it contains are intended for sale individually

codes.heading: Multiple-component retail product, loose
codes.notes: Format of product components must be given in <ProductPart>

codes.heading: Multiple-component retail product, part(s) enclosed
codes.notes: Multiple component product where subsidiary product part(s) is / are supplied as enclosures to the primary part, eg a book with a CD packaged in a sleeve glued within the back cover. Format of product components must be given in <ProductPart>

codes.heading: Multiple-component retail product, entirely digital
codes.notes: Multiple component product where all parts are digital, and delivered as separate files, eg a group of individual EPUB files, an EPUB with a PDF, an e-book with a license to access a range of online resources, etc. Format of product components must be given in <ProductPart>

codes.heading: Multiple-component retail product, partly digital
codes.notes: Multiple component product where some parts are digital, but at least one is physical, eg a physical book with a digital version also included, or an educational product containing a mix of physical and digital material. Format of product components must be given in <ProductPart>

codes.heading: Video
codes.notes: Video – detail unspecified. Use only when the form is unknown and no further detail can be provided. Prefer VZ plus <ProductFormDescription> if detail is available but no other V* code applies

codes.heading: Videodisc
codes.notes: eg Laserdisc

codes.heading: DVD video
codes.notes: DVD video: specify TV standard in <ProductFormDetail>

codes.heading: VHS video
codes.notes: VHS videotape: specify TV standard in <ProductFormDetail>

codes.heading: Betamax video
codes.notes: Betamax videotape: specify TV standard in <ProductFormDetail>

codes.heading: VCD
codes.notes: VideoCD

codes.heading: SVCD
codes.notes: Super VideoCD

codes.heading: HD DVD
codes.notes: High definition DVD disc, Toshiba HD DVD format

codes.heading: Blu-ray
codes.notes: High definition DVD disc, Sony Blu-ray format

codes.heading: UMD Video
codes.notes: Sony Universal Media disc

codes.heading: CBHD
codes.notes: China Blue High-Definition, derivative of HD-DVD

codes.heading: Other video format
codes.notes: Other video format not specified by VB to VQ. Further detail is expected in <ProductFormDescription>, as <ProductFormDetail> and <ProductFormFeature> are unlikely to be sufficient

codes.heading: Trade-only material
codes.notes: Trade-only material (unspecified). Use only when the form is unknown and no further detail can be provided. Prefer XZ plus <ProductFormDescription> if detail is available but no other X* code applies

codes.heading: Dumpbin – filled
codes.notes: Dumpbin with contents. ISBN (where applicable) and format of contained items must be given in <ProductPart>

codes.heading: Counterpack – filled
codes.notes: Counterpack with contents. ISBN (where applicable) and format of contained items must be given in <ProductPart>

codes.heading: Poster, promotional
codes.notes: Promotional poster for display, not for sale – see also PK

codes.heading: Window piece
codes.notes: Promotional piece for shop window display

codes.heading: Large book display
codes.notes: Large scale facsimile of book for promotional display

codes.heading: Shrink-wrapped pack
codes.notes: A quantity pack with its own product code, usually for trade supply only: the retail items it contains are intended for sale individually. ISBN (where applicable) and format of contained items must be given in <ProductPart>. For products or product bundles supplied individually shrink-wrapped for retail sale, use code SD

codes.heading: Boxed pack
codes.notes: A quantity pack with its own product code, usually for trade supply only: the retail items it contains are intended for sale individually. ISBN (where applicable) and format of contained items must be given in <ProductPart>. For products or product bundles boxed individually for retail sale, use code SB

codes.heading: Pack (outer packaging unspecified)
codes.notes: A quantity pack with its own product code, usually for trade supply only: the retail items it contains are intended for sale individually. ISBN (where applicable) and format of contained items must be given in <ProductPart>. Use only when the pack is neither shrinp-wrapped nor boxed

codes.heading: Spinner – filled
codes.notes: Spinner with contents. ISBN(s) (where applicable) and detail of contained items must be given in <ProductPart>

codes.heading: Other point of sale – including retail product
codes.notes: Other point of sale material not specified by XB to XO, supplied with included product(s) for retail sale. The retail product(s) must be described in <ProductPart>. Further detail of the POS material is expected in <ProductFormDescription>, as <ProductFormDetail> and <ProductFormFeature> are unlikely to be sufficient

codes.heading: Other point of sale
codes.notes: Other point of sale material not specified by XB to XY, promotional or decorative. Further detail is expected in <ProductFormDescription>, as <ProductFormDetail> and <ProductFormFeature> are unlikely to be sufficient

codes.heading: General merchandise
codes.notes: General merchandise, book accessories and non-book products – unspecified. Use only when the form is unknown and no further detail can be provided. Prefer ZX, ZY or ZZ, plus <ProductFormDescription> if detail is available but no other Z* code applies

codes.heading: Doll or figure
codes.notes: Including action figures, figurines

codes.heading: Soft toy
codes.notes: Soft or plush toy

codes.heading: Toy
codes.notes: Including educational toys (where no other code is relevant)

codes.heading: Game
codes.notes: Board game, or other game (except computer game: see DE and other D* codes)

codes.heading: E-book reader
codes.notes: Dedicated e-book reading device, typically with mono screen

codes.heading: Tablet computer
codes.notes: General purpose tablet computer, typically with color screen

codes.heading: Audiobook player
codes.notes: Dedicated audiobook player device, typically including book-related features like bookmarking

codes.heading: Jigsaw
codes.notes: Jigsaw or similar ‘shapes’ puzzle

codes.heading: Mug
codes.notes: For example, branded, promotional or tie-in drinking mug, cup etc

codes.heading: Tote bag
codes.notes: For example, branded, promotional or tie-in bag

codes.heading: Tableware
codes.notes: For example, branded, promotional or tie-in plates, bowls etc (note for mugs and cups, use code ZK)

codes.heading: Umbrella
codes.notes: For example, branded, promotional or tie-in umbrella

codes.heading: Paints, crayons, pencils
codes.notes: Coloring set, including pens, chalks, etc

codes.heading: Handicraft kit
codes.notes: Handicraft kit or set, eg sewing, crochet, weaving, basketry, beadwork, leather, wood or metalworking, pottery and glassworking, candlemaking etc

codes.heading: Other toy / game accessories
codes.notes: Other toy, game and puzzle items not specified by ZB to ZQ, generally accessories to other products etc. Further detail is expected in <ProductFormDescription>, as <ProductFormDetail> and <ProductFormFeature> are unlikely to be sufficient

codes.heading: Other apparel
codes.notes: Other apparel items not specified by ZB to ZQ, including branded, promotional or tie-in scarves, caps, aprons, dress-up costumes etc. Further detail is expected in <ProductFormDescription>, as <ProductFormDetail> and <ProductFormFeature> are unlikely to be sufficient

codes.heading: Other merchandise
codes.notes: Other branded, promotional or tie-in merchandise not specified by ZB to ZY. Further detail is expected in <ProductFormDescription>, as <ProductFormDetail> and <ProductFormFeature> are unlikely to be sufficient

codes.heading: Publication date
codes.notes: Nominal date of publication. This date is primarily used for planning, promotion and other business process purposes, and is not necessarily the first date for retail sales or fulfillment of pre-orders. In the absence of a sales embargo date, retail sales and pre-order fulfillment may begin as soon as stock is available to the retailer

codes.heading: Sales embargo date
codes.notes: If there is an embargo on retail sales (in the market) before a certain date, the date from which the embargo is lifted and retail sales and fulfillment of pre-orders are permitted. (In some markets, this may be termed a ‘strict on-sale date’.) The embargo applies equally to previews, unless a separate preview embargo is also provided. In the absence of an embargo date, previews, retail sales and pre-order fulfillment may begin as soon as stock is available to the retailer

codes.heading: Public announcement date
codes.notes: Date when a new product may be announced to the general public. Prior to the announcement date, the product data is intended for internal use by the recipient and supply chain partners only. After the announcement date, or in the absence of an announcement date, the planned product may be announced to the public as soon as metadata is available

codes.heading: Trade announcement date
codes.notes: Date when a new product may be announced to the book trade only. Prior to the announcement date, the product information is intended for internal use by the recipient only. After the announcement date, or in the absence of a trade announcement date, the planned product may be announced to supply chain partners (but not necessarily made public – see the Public announcement date) as soon as metadata is available

codes.heading: Date of first publication
codes.notes: Date when the work incorporated in a product was first published. For works in translation, see also Date of first publication in original language (code 20)

codes.heading: Latest reprint date
codes.notes: Date when a product was most recently reprinted

codes.heading: Out-of-print / permanently withdrawn date
codes.notes: Date when a product was (or will be) declared out-of-print, permanently withdrawn from sale or deleted

codes.heading: Latest reissue date
codes.notes: Date when a product was most recently reissued

codes.heading: Publication date of print counterpart
codes.notes: Date of publication of a printed book which is the direct print counterpart to a digital product. The counterpart product may be included in <RelatedProduct> using code 13

codes.heading: Date of first publication in original language
codes.notes: Date when the original language version of the work incorporated in a product was first published (note, use only on works in translation – and also see code 11 for the first publication date of the translation)

codes.heading: Forthcoming reissue date
codes.notes: Date when a product will be reissued

codes.heading: Expected availability date after temporary withdrawal
codes.notes: Date when a product that has been temporary withdrawn from sale or recalled for any reason is expected to become available again, eg after correction of quality or technical issues

codes.heading: Review embargo date
codes.notes: Date from which reviews of a product may be published eg in newspapers and magazines or online. Provided to the book trade for information only: newspapers and magazines are not expected to be recipients of ONIX metadata

codes.heading: Publisher’s reservation order deadline
codes.notes: Latest date on which an order may be placed with the publisher for guaranteed delivery prior to the publication date. May or may not be linked to a special reservation or pre-publication price

codes.heading: Forthcoming reprint date
codes.notes: Date when a product will be reprinted

codes.heading: Preorder embargo date
codes.notes: Earliest date a retail ‘preorder’ can be placed (in the market), where this is distinct from the public announcement date. In the absence of a preorder embargo, advance orders can be placed as soon as metadata is available to the consumer (this would be the public announcement date, or in the absence of a public announcement date, the earliest date metadata is available to the retailer)

codes.heading: Transfer date
codes.notes: Date of acquisition of product by new publisher (use with publishing roles 09 and 13)

codes.heading: Date of production
codes.notes: For an audiovisual work (eg on DVD)

codes.heading: Streaming embargo date
codes.notes: For digital products that are available to end customers both as a download and streamed, the earliest date the product can be made available on a stream, where the streamed version becomes available later than the download. For the download, see code 02 if it is embargoed or code 01 if there is no embargo

codes.heading: Subscription embargo date
codes.notes: For digital products that are available to end customers both as purchases and as part of a subscription package, the earliest date the product can be made available by subscription, where the product may not be included in a subscription package until some while after publication. For ordinary sales, see code 02 if there is a sales embargo or code 01 if there is no embargo

codes.heading: Download embargo date
codes.notes: For digital products that are available to end customers both as a download and streamed, the earliest date the product can be made available via download, where the download version becomes available later than the stream. For any embargo on the stream, see code 02

codes.heading: Purchase embargo date
codes.notes: For digital products that are available to end customers both as purchases and as part of a subscription package, the earliest date the product can be made available to purchase, where the product may not be purchased until some while after it becomes available via the subscription. For any embargo on the subscription, see code 02

codes.heading: CIP date
codes.notes: Date by which CIP copy is required for inclusion in the product

codes.heading: Date of first unabridged publication
codes.notes: Date when the unabridged version of the work incorporated in a product was first published (note, use only on abridged works – and also see code 11 for the first publication date of the abridgement)

codes.heading: Year of publication
codes.notes: Where this is managed separately from the date of publication (code 01), for example for library use. Note, requires an explicit dateformat code 05 attribute (YYYY)

codes.heading: Preview embargo date
codes.notes: Date from which previews of a product may be made available, where the embargo is managed separately from any Sales embargo date. Applies to all previews (previews in <TextContent> or <SupportingResource>, previews covered by <EpubUsageConstraint> and external preview ‘widgets’) UNLESS overridden by a Valid from date for a specific preview

codes.heading: Library embargo date
codes.notes: For digital products that are available to end customers both via retail sale and sales to libraries, the earliest date the product can be made available to purchase by libraries, or made available by a library to patrons. For any embargo on non-library sales, see code 02

codes.heading: Availability embargo date
codes.notes: The earliest date on which the book may be released from a distributor’s or wholesaler’s warehouse (ie an embargo on the expected availability date)

codes.heading: Manuscript submission date
codes.notes: Date of submission of the completed manuscript to the publisher, prior to review. Typically for academic and scholarly publishing

codes.heading: Manuscript accepted date
codes.notes: Date of acceptance of the final completed manuscript by the publisher, after review but before final preparation for publication. Typically for academic and scholarly publishing

codes.heading: CD standard audio format
codes.notes: CD ‘red book’ format

codes.heading: MP3 format
codes.notes: MPEG-1/2 Audio Layer III file

codes.heading: WMA
codes.notes: Windows Media Audio format

codes.heading: AAC
codes.notes: Advanced Audio Coding format

codes.heading: Ogg/Vorbis
codes.notes: Vorbis audio format in the Ogg container

codes.heading: Audible
codes.notes: Audio format proprietary to Audible.com

codes.heading: FLAC
codes.notes: Free lossless audio codec

codes.heading: AIFF
codes.notes: Audio Interchangeable File Format

codes.heading: ALAC
codes.notes: Apple Lossless Audio Codec

codes.heading: W3C Audiobook format
codes.notes: Audiobook package format

codes.heading: DAISY 2: full audio with navigation (no text)
DAISY 2: full audio with navigation and partial text
DAISY 2: full audio with navigation and full text
DAISY 2: full text with navigation and partial audio
codes.notes: Reading systems may provide full audio via text-to-speech

codes.heading: DAISY 2: full text with navigation and no audio
codes.notes: Reading systems may provide full audio via text-to-speech

codes.heading: DAISY 3: full audio with navigation (no text)
DAISY 3: full audio with navigation and partial text
DAISY 3: full audio with navigation and full text
DAISY 3: full text with navigation and partial audio
codes.notes: Reading systems may provide full audio via text-to-speech

codes.heading: DAISY 3: full text with navigation and no audio
codes.notes: Reading systems may provide full audio via text-to-speech

codes.heading: Readalong audio
codes.notes: Audio intended exclusively for use alongside a printed copy of the book. Most often a children’s product. Normally contains instructions such as ‘turn the page now’ and other references to the printed item, and is usually sold packaged together with a printed copy

codes.heading: Playalong audio
codes.notes: Audio intended for musical accompaniment, eg ‘Music minus one’, etc, often used for music learning. Includes singalong backing audio for musical learning or for Karaoke-style entertainment

codes.heading: Speakalong audio
codes.notes: Audio intended for language learning, which includes speech plus gaps intended to be filled by the listener

codes.heading: Synchronized audio
codes.notes: Audio synchronized to text within an e-publication, for example an EPUB3 with audio overlay. Synchronization at least at paragraph level, and covering the full content

codes.heading: Sound effects
codes.notes: Incidental sounds added to the audiobook narration (eg background environmental sounds)

codes.heading: Background music
codes.notes: Incidental music added to the audiobook narration (eg to heighten atmosphere). Do not use where the music is a primary part of the audio

codes.heading: Without background sounds
codes.notes: Pre-recorded audiobook narration does not contain any background sounds, including music, sound effects, etc, though music and effects may be present if isolated from the speech (ie the sounds do not overlap)

codes.heading: 64kbits/s
codes.notes: Constant or average bit rate (eg of an mp3 or AAC audio file) 64kbits/second or more. Note the bit rate is the total across all channels, not a per channel rate

codes.heading: 128kbits/s
codes.notes: Constant or average bit rate 128bbits/second or more

codes.heading: Mono
codes.notes: Includes ‘stereo’ where channels are identical

codes.heading: Stereo
codes.notes: Includes ‘joint stereo’

codes.heading: Stereo 2.1
codes.notes: Stereo plus low-frequency channel

codes.heading: Surround 4.1
codes.notes: Five-channel audio (including low-frequency channel)

codes.heading: Surround 5.1
codes.notes: Six-channel audio (including low-frequency channel)

codes.heading: Dolby Atmos
codes.notes: Multi-channel ‘spatial’ audio (eg for 7.1.4 speaker arrangements or processed for headphone delivery)

codes.heading: Mass market (rack) paperback
codes.notes: In North America, a category of paperback characterized partly by page size (typically from 6¾ up to 7⅛ x 4¼ inches) and partly by target market and terms of trade. Use with Product Form code BC

codes.heading: Trade paperback (US)
codes.notes: In North America, a category of paperback characterized partly by page size (larger than rack-sized) and partly by target market and terms of trade. AKA ‘quality paperback’, and including textbooks. Most paperback books sold in North America except ‘mass-market’ (B101) and ‘tall rack’ (B107) are correctly described with this code. Use with Product Form code BC

codes.heading: Digest format paperback
codes.notes: In North America, a category of paperback characterized by page size (typically 7 x 5 inches) and generally used for children’s books; use with Product Form code BC. Note: was wrongly shown as B102 (duplicate entry) in Issue 3

codes.heading: A-format paperback
codes.notes: In UK and IE, a category of paperback characterized by page size (normally 178 x 111 mm approx); use with Product Form code BC

codes.heading: B-format paperback
codes.notes: In UK and IE, a category of paperback characterized by page size (normally 198 x 129 mm approx); use with Product Form code BC

codes.heading: Trade paperback (UK)
codes.notes: In UK and IE, a category of paperback characterized largely by size (usually in traditional hardback dimensions), and often used for paperback originals or retailer / travel / export-exclusives; use with Product Form code BC

codes.heading: Tall rack paperback (US)
codes.notes: In North America, a category of paperback characterized partly by page size (typically 7½ x 4¼ inches) and partly by target market and terms of trade; use with Product Form code BC

codes.heading: A5 size Tankobon
codes.notes: Japanese A-series size, 210 x 148mm. A tankobon is a complete collected story originally published in serialized form (eg in a magazine)

codes.heading: JIS B5 size Tankobon
codes.notes: Japanese B-series size, 257 x 182mm

codes.heading: JIS B6 size Tankobon
codes.notes: Japanese B-series size, 182 x 128mm

codes.heading: A6 size Bunko
codes.notes: Japanese A-series size, 148 x 105mm

codes.heading: B40-dori Shinsho
codes.notes: Japanese format, 182x103mm or 173x105mm

codes.heading: Pocket (Sweden, Norway, France)
codes.notes: A Swedish, Norwegian, French paperback format, of no particular fixed size. Use with Product Form Code BC

codes.heading: Storpocket (Sweden)
codes.notes: A Swedish paperback format, use with Product Form Code BC. In Finnish, Jättipokkari

codes.heading: Kartonnage (Sweden)
codes.notes: A Swedish hardback format, use with Product Form Code BB

codes.heading: Flexband (Sweden)
codes.notes: A Swedish softback format, use with Product Form Code BC

codes.heading: Mook / Bookazine
codes.notes: A softback book in the format of a magazine, usually sold like a book. Use with Product Form code BC

codes.heading: Dwarsligger
codes.notes: Also called ‘Flipback’. A softback book in a specially compact proprietary format with pages printed in landscape on very thin paper and bound along the long (top) edge (ie parallel with the lines of text). Use with Product Form code BC – see www.dwarsligger.com

codes.heading: 46 size
codes.notes: Japanese format, 188 x 127mm

codes.heading: 46-Henkei size
codes.notes: Japanese format, approximately 188 x 127mm

codes.heading: A4-Henkei size
codes.notes: Japanese format, approximately 297 x 210mm

codes.heading: A5-Henkei size
codes.notes: Japanese format, approximately 210 x 146mm

codes.heading: B5-Henkei size
codes.notes: Japanese format, approximately 257 x 182mm

codes.heading: B6-Henkei size
codes.notes: Japanese format, approximately 182 x 128mm

codes.heading: JIS B7 size
codes.notes: Japanese B-series size, 128 x 91mm

codes.heading: Kiku size
codes.notes: Japanese format, 218 x 152mm or 227 x 152mm

codes.heading: Kiku-Henkei size
codes.notes: Japanese format

codes.heading: JIS B4 size
codes.notes: Japanese B-series size, 364 x 257 mm

codes.heading: Paperback (DE)
codes.notes: German large paperback format, greater than about 205mm high, with flaps. Use with Product form code BC

codes.heading: Libro de bolsillo
codes.notes: Spanish pocket paperback. Use with Product form code BC

codes.heading: Pocket-sized
codes.notes: Pocket-sized format, usually less than about 205mm high, without necessarily implying a particular trade category (de: ,Taschenbuch‘; it: «Tascabile / Supertascabile»; es: «libro de bolsillo»; fr: « livre de poche » etc). Use with Product form code BB or BC. See also List 12 code 04

codes.heading: Mass market max paperback
codes.notes: In North America, a category of paperback characterized partly by page size (typically 7⅛ x 4¾ inches) and partly by target market and terms of trade. Use with Product Form code BC

codes.heading: Comic book size (US)
codes.notes: Standard 10.25 x 6.625in size approx (260 x 170mm)

codes.heading: Comic album size (Euro)
codes.notes: Standard 240 x 320mm size approx

codes.heading: B4-Henkei size
codes.notes: Japanese format, approximately 364 x 257 mm

codes.heading: Touch-and-feel book
codes.notes: Sensory book. A book whose pages have a variety of textured inserts designed to stimulate tactile exploration: see also B214 and B215

codes.heading: Die-cut book
codes.notes: A book which is cut into a distinctive non-rectilinear shape and/or in which holes or shapes have been cut internally. (‘Die-cut’ is used here as a convenient shorthand, and does not imply strict limitation to a particular production process)

codes.heading: Book-as-toy
codes.notes: A book which is also a toy, or which incorporates a toy as an integral part. (Do not, however, use B213 for a multiple-item product which includes a book and a toy as separate items)

codes.heading: Soft-to-touch book
codes.notes: A book whose cover has a soft textured finish, typically over board

codes.heading: Fuzzy-felt book
codes.notes: A book with detachable felt pieces and textured pages on which they can be arranged

codes.heading: Press-out pieces
codes.notes: A book containing pages with die-cut or press-out pieces that can be used as a jigsaw, as puzzle or game pieces, play pieces (eg paper dolls) etc

codes.heading: Picture book
codes.notes: Picture book, generally for children though also occasionally for teens or adults, with few words per illustration: use with applicable Product form code

codes.heading: ‘Carousel’ book
codes.notes: (aka ‘Star’ book). Tax treatment of products may differ from that of products with similar codes such as Book as toy or Pop-up book)

codes.heading: Pull-the-tab book
codes.notes: A book with movable card ‘tabs’ within the pages. Pull a tab to reveal or animate part of a picture (distinct from a ‘lift-the-flap’ book, where flaps simply reveal hidden pictures, and not specifically a ‘pop-up’ book with 3D paper engineering – though when combined with code B206 indicates a pop-up book with tabs for moveable parts of 3D ‘scenes’)

codes.heading: ‘Wordless’ book
codes.notes: Picture book, generally for children though also used in augmentative and alternative education, or for teens and adults, without text in the body of the book. Also ‘silent books’, wordless graphic novels and comic books: use with applicable Product Form code

codes.heading: Cut-out pieces
codes.notes: A book containing pages with pieces intended to be cut out (not pre-cut or press-out – see B216) that can be used as puzzle or game pieces, play pieces etc, but which may not be suitable for young children

codes.heading: Loose leaf or partwork – sheets / parts and binder / wallet
codes.notes: Use with Product Form code BD, BN or PM

codes.heading: Loose leaf or partwork – binder / wallet only
codes.notes: Use with Product Form code BD, BN or PM

codes.heading: Loose leaf or partwork – sheets / parts only
codes.notes: Use with Product Form code BD, BN or PM

codes.heading: Sewn
codes.notes: AKA stitched; for ‘saddle-sewn’, prefer code B310

codes.heading: Unsewn / adhesive bound
codes.notes: Including ‘perfect bound’, ‘glued’

codes.heading: Library binding
codes.notes: Strengthened cloth-over-boards binding intended for libraries: use with Product form code BB

codes.heading: Reinforced binding
codes.notes: Strengthened binding, not specifically intended for libraries: use with Product form code BB or BC

codes.heading: Half bound
codes.notes: Highest quality material used on spine and corners only. Must be accompanied by a code specifying a material, eg ‘half-bound real leather’

codes.heading: Quarter bound
codes.notes: Highest quality material used on spine only. Must be accompanied by a code specifying a material, eg ‘quarter bound real leather’

codes.heading: Saddle-sewn
codes.notes: AKA ‘saddle-stitched’ or ‘wire-stitched’

codes.heading: Comb bound
codes.notes: Round or oval plastic forms in a clamp-like configuration: use with Product Form code BE

codes.heading: Wire-O
codes.notes: Twin loop metal wire spine: use with Product Form code BE

codes.heading: Concealed wire
codes.notes: Cased over Coiled or Wire-O binding: use with Product Form code BE and Product Form Detail code B312 or B314

codes.heading: Coiled wire bound
codes.notes: Spiral wire bound. Use with product form code BE. The default if a spiral binding type is not stated. Cf. Comb and Wire-O binding

codes.heading: Trade binding
codes.notes: Hardcover binding intended for general consumers rather than libraries, use with Product form code BB. The default if a hardcover binding detail is not stated. cf. Library binding

codes.heading: Swiss binding
codes.notes: Cover is attached to the book block along only one edge of the spine, allowing the cover to lay flat

codes.heading: Notched binding
codes.notes: Refinement of perfect binding, with notches cut in the spine of the book block prior to glueing, to improve adhesion and durability

codes.heading: Lay-flat binding
codes.notes: Hardcover or softcover where interior spreads lay flat across the spine

codes.heading: Flush cut binding
codes.notes: Hardcover where the cover boards are trimmed flush with the trimmed book block

codes.heading: Rounded spine
codes.notes: Hardcover where the spine is rounded during binding

codes.heading: Square spine
codes.notes: Hardcover where the spine is straight

codes.heading: Self-covered
codes.notes: Covers do not use a distinctive stock, but are the same as the body pages. Use for example with Product form BF, to indicate a pamphlet does not use a card or distinct paper cover. See also B416 (for card covers) and B418 (for distinct paper covers)

codes.heading: Cloth over boards
codes.notes: Cotton, linen or other woven fabric over boards. Use with <ProductForm> BB

codes.heading: Paper over boards
codes.notes: Cellulose-based or similar non-woven material, which may be printed and may be embossed with an artificial cloth or leather-like texture, over boards. Use for example with <ProductForm> BB, to distinguish from B401, or with BE to specify the covers of a spiral-bound book. See also B400 (for self-covers) and B416 (for card covers)

codes.heading: Leather, real
codes.notes: Covered with leather created by tanning animal hide. May be ‘full-grain’ using the entire thickness of the hide, ‘top grain’ using the outer layer of the hide, or ‘split’ using the inner layers of the hide. Split leather may be embossed with an artificial grain or texture. Use with <ProductForm> BG, and if appropriate with codes B308 or B309 (otherwise ‘full-bound’ is implied)

codes.heading: Leather, imitation
codes.notes: Covered with synthetic leather-like material – polymer or non-animal fibre over a textile backing, usually coated and embossed with an artificial grain or texture. Leatherette, pleather etc. Use with <ProductForm> BB (or BG if particularly high-quality), and if appropriate with codes B308 or B309 (otherwise ‘full-bound’ is implied)

codes.heading: Leather, bonded
codes.notes: Covered with leather reconstituted from a pulp made from shredded animal hide, layered on a fibre or textile backing, coated and usually embossed with an artificial grain or texture. Use with <ProductForm> BG, and if appropriate with codes B308 or B309 (otherwise ‘full-bound’ is implied)

codes.heading: Vellum
codes.notes: Pages made with prepared but untanned animal skin (usually calf, occasionally goat or sheep). Includes parchment, a thicker and less refined form of animal skin, but not ‘paper vellum’ or vegetable parchment made from synthetic or plant fibres

codes.heading: Head and tail bands
codes.notes: Capital bands, either decorative or functional. Use <ProductFormFeature> to specify the color

codes.heading: Decorated page edges
codes.notes: Colored, stained, gilded, patterned, abstract or illustrated sprayed edges. Use <ProductFormFeature> to specify the color, and optionally, use <SupportingResource> to provide an image of the decoration

codes.heading: Decorated endpapers
codes.notes: Colored, patterned, printed, abstract or illustrated endpapers or of inside front and back covers. Use <ProductFormFeature> to specify the color, and optionally, use <SupportingResource> to provide an image of the decoration

codes.heading: Cloth
codes.notes: Cloth, not necessarily over boards – cf B401

codes.heading: Imitation cloth
codes.notes: Spanish ‘simil-tela’

codes.heading: Flexible plastic / vinyl cover
codes.notes: AKA ‘flexibound’: use with Product Form code BC

codes.heading: Plastic-covered
codes.notes: Separate outer plastic cover, often transparent and allowing the cover to show through. Typically has pockets into which the cover tucks. See also B412, where the cover itself is plastic or vinyl

codes.heading: Vinyl-covered
codes.notes: Separate outer vinyl cover. See also B412, where the cover itself is plastic or vinyl

codes.heading: Laminated cover
codes.notes: Book, laminating material unspecified, often termed PLC or PPC (printed laminated case, printed paper case) when used with Product form BB. Use L101 for ‘whole product laminated’, eg a laminated sheet map or wallchart

codes.heading: Card cover
codes.notes: With card cover (like a typical paperback). As distinct from a self-cover or more elaborate board binding. Use for example with Product forms BE or BF, to indicate a spiral-bound book or pamphlet is bound within a card cover. See also B400 (for self-covers) and B418 (for distinct paper covers), B401 or B402 (for board covers)

codes.heading: Duplex-printed cover
codes.notes: Printed both inside and outside the front and/or back cover

codes.heading: Paper cover
codes.notes: Cover uses a distinct, usually heavier (thicker) paper than the interior pages. Use for example with Product form BF, to indicate a pamphlet is bound within a paper cover. See also B400 (for self-covers) and B416 (for card covers)

codes.heading: Delicate cover / jacket finish
codes.notes: Cover or jacket finish may merit special handling or packaging during distribution and fulfilment, for example because of gloss varnish which may hold fingerprints or matt laminate liable to scuffing

codes.heading: Embossed cover
codes.notes: Embossing (or debossing) used on cover or jacket

codes.heading: Temporary stickers on cover or jacket
codes.notes: All types of promotional stickers, applied on behalf of the publisher, but easily removable by the reader without damage to the cover or jacket

codes.heading: Permanent stickers on cover or jacket
codes.notes: All types of promotional stickers, applied on behalf of the publisher, but not capable of being removed easily without damage to the cover or jacket

codes.heading: Spine panorama
codes.notes: Spine illustration combines with spines of other products in a collection to form a panoramic image. Sometimes termed a ‘spinescape’

codes.heading: Belly band
codes.notes: Obi. Paper band around the middle of a book (typically tucked inside the front and back cover rather than extending around the whole book)

codes.heading: With dust jacket
codes.notes: Type unspecified

codes.heading: With printed dust jacket
codes.notes: Used to distinguish from B503

codes.heading: With translucent dust cover
codes.notes: With translucent paper or plastic protective cover

codes.heading: With flaps
codes.notes: For paperback with flaps – sometimes known as gatefolds or French flaps (extensions of the cover that fold inside the front and back cover)

codes.heading: With ribbon marker(s)
codes.notes: If the number of markers is significant, it can be stated as free text in <ProductFormDescription>. Use <ProductFormFeature> to specify the color

codes.heading: With leather edge lining
codes.notes: AKA yapp edge?

codes.heading: Rough front
codes.notes: With edge trimming such that the front edge is ragged, not neatly and squarely trimmed: AKA deckle edge, feather edge, uncut edge, rough cut

codes.heading: Foldout
codes.notes: With one or more gatefold or foldout sections bound into the book block

codes.heading: Wide margin
codes.notes: Pages include extra-wide margin specifically intended for hand-written annotations

codes.heading: With fastening strap
codes.notes: Book with attached loop for fixing to baby stroller, cot, chair etc

codes.heading: With perforated pages
codes.notes: With one or more pages perforated and intended to be torn out for use

codes.heading: Acid-free paper
codes.notes: Printed on acid-free or alkaline buffered paper conforming with ISO 9706

codes.heading: Archival paper
codes.notes: Printed on acid-free or alkaline buffered paper with a high cotton content, conforming with ISO 11108

codes.heading: With elasticated strap
codes.notes: Strap acts as closure or as page marker

codes.heading: With serialized authenticity token
codes.notes: For example, holographic sticker such as the banderol used in the Turkish book trade

codes.heading: With dust jacket poster
codes.notes: Jacket in the form of a pamphlet or poster, specifically intended to be removed and read or used separately from the book

codes.heading: Rounded corners
codes.notes: Usually die-cut rounding to foredge corners of cover (and/or to foredge page corners). See B212 for elaborate die-cutting

codes.heading: Splashproof
codes.notes: Water-resistant or ‘waterproof’ cover and pages

codes.heading: Mineral paper
codes.notes: Pages composed of ‘mineral paper’ comprised of HDPE plastic and ground calcium carbonate, eg Stonepaper

codes.heading: With accessibility claim ticket
codes.notes: For example, cut-out claim form such as the ‘text data request ticket’ used in the Japanese book trade

codes.heading: Plastic paper
codes.notes: Pages composed of microporous sheets comprised of non-woven HDPE or HDPP fibers, or of non-porous HDPP film, eg Tyvek or Yupo

codes.heading: With wraparound foredge flap
codes.notes: For paperback with flaps (an extension of the cover that folds outside the front or back cover, covering the foredge). The other flap may be absent, conventional or may also wrap around the foredge

codes.heading: Turn-around book
codes.notes: A book in which half the content is printed upside-down, to be read the other way round. Also known as a ‘flip-book’ or ‘tête-bêche’ (Fr) binding, it has two front covers and a single spine. Usually an omnibus of two works

codes.heading: Unflipped manga format
codes.notes: Manga with pages and panels in the sequence of (right-to-left flowing) Japanese-style design

codes.heading: Back-to-back book
codes.notes: A book in which half the content is printed so as to be read from the other cover. All content is printed the same way up. Also known as ‘dos-à-dos’ (Fr) binding, it has two front covers and two spines. Usually an omnibus of two works

codes.heading: Flipped manga format
codes.notes: Manga with pages and panels in the sequence mirrored from Japanese-style design (thus flowing left-to-right)

codes.heading: Variant turn-around book
codes.notes: A book in which half the content is read the other way round from ‘back’ to ‘front’. A variant on ‘flip-book’ or ‘tête-bêche’ (fr) binding where the text is in two languages with different page progression (eg English and Arabic) and neither needs to be upside down, it has two front covers and a single spine. Usually an omnibus of a work and a derived translated work

codes.heading: Page progression LTR
codes.notes: Pages are ordered left to right (the left page in a spread is read before the right). Note this does not specifically mean text on the page is also read left to right

codes.heading: Page progression RTL
codes.notes: Pages are ordered right to left

codes.heading: Page progression TTB
codes.notes: Pages are ordered top to bottom, with the spine oriented horizontally. See also Dwarsligger (code B118), a proprietary variation of this format

codes.heading: Page progression other
codes.notes: Pages are ordered bottom to top, with the spine oriented horizontally, or in a way for which there is no other code

codes.heading: Syllabification
codes.notes: Text shows syllable breaks

codes.heading: Upper case only
codes.notes: For bicameral scripts, body text is upper case only

codes.heading: UK Uncontracted Braille
codes.notes: Single letters only. Was formerly identified as UK Braille Grade 1

codes.heading: UK Contracted Braille
codes.notes: With some letter combinations. Was formerly identified as UK Braille Grade 2

codes.heading: US Braille
codes.notes: For US Braille, prefer codes B704 and B705 as appropriate

codes.heading: Unified English Braille
codes.notes: For UEB, prefer codes B708 and B709 as appropriate

codes.heading: Moon
codes.notes: Moon embossed alphabet, used by some print-impaired readers who have difficulties with Braille

codes.heading: Tactile images
codes.notes: Eg charts, diagrams, maps, or other tactile graphics or illustrations that are embossed or textured for accessibility purposes

codes.heading: Lenticular images
codes.notes: Image-changing effect, ‘3D’ images, ‘tilt cards’, printed with tiny lenses

codes.heading: Anaglyph images
codes.notes: Stereoscopic 3D effect (eg of images) as viewed through red / green filters

codes.heading: Raised 3D relief
codes.notes: Physical 3D relief (eg of a map, globe) reflects height of terrain etc

codes.heading: Real Video format
codes.notes: Proprietary RealNetworks format. Includes Real Video packaged within a .rm RealMedia container

codes.heading: EPUB

codes.heading: OEB

codes.heading: DOC

codes.heading: DOCX

codes.heading: HTML

codes.heading: ODF

codes.heading: PDF
codes.notes: Portable Document Format (ISO 32000-1:2008) [File extension .pdf]

codes.heading: PDF/A
codes.notes: PDF archiving format defined by ISO 19005-1:2005 [File extension .pdf]

codes.heading: RTF
codes.notes: Rich Text Format [File extension .rtf]

codes.heading: SGML
codes.notes: Standard Generalized Mark-up Language

codes.heading: TCR
codes.notes: A compressed text format mainly used on Psion handheld devices [File extension .tcr]

codes.heading: TXT
codes.notes: Text file format [File extension .txt]. Typically ASCII or Unicode UTF-8 / 16

codes.heading: XHTML
codes.notes: Extensible Hypertext Markup Language [File extension .xhtml, .xht, .xml, .html, .htm]

codes.heading: zTXT
codes.notes: A compressed text format mainly used on Palm handheld devices [File extension .pdb – see also E121, E125, E130]

codes.heading: XPS
codes.notes: XML Paper Specification format [File extension .xps]

codes.heading: Amazon Kindle
codes.notes: A format proprietary to Amazon for use with its Kindle reading devices or software readers [File extensions .azw, .mobi, .prc etc]. Prefer code E148 for Print Replica files

codes.heading: BBeB
codes.notes: A Sony proprietary format for use with the Sony Reader and LIBRIé reading devices [File extension .lrf]

codes.heading: DXReader
codes.notes: A proprietary format for use with DXReader software

codes.heading: EBL
codes.notes: A format proprietary to the Ebook Library service

codes.heading: Ebrary
codes.notes: A format proprietary to the Ebrary service

codes.heading: eReader
codes.notes: A proprietary format for use with eReader (AKA ‘Palm Reader’) software on various hardware platforms [File extension .pdb – see also E114, E125, E130]

codes.heading: Exebook
codes.notes: A proprietary format with its own reading system for Windows platforms [File extension .exe]

codes.heading: Franklin eBookman
codes.notes: A proprietary format for use with the Franklin eBookman reader

codes.heading: Gemstar Rocketbook
codes.notes: A proprietary format for use with the Gemstar Rocketbook reader [File extension .rb]

codes.heading: iSilo
codes.notes: A proprietary format for use with iSilo software on various hardware platforms [File extension .pdb – see also E114, E121, E130]

codes.heading: Microsoft Reader
codes.notes: A proprietary format for use with Microsoft Reader software on Windows and Pocket PC platforms [File extension .lit]

codes.heading: Mobipocket
codes.notes: A proprietary format for use with Mobipocket software on various hardware platforms [File extensions .mobi, .prc]. Includes Amazon Kindle formats up to and including version 7 – but prefer code E116 for version 7, and always use E116 for KF8

codes.heading: MyiLibrary
codes.notes: A format proprietary to the MyiLibrary service

codes.heading: NetLibrary
codes.notes: A format proprietary to the NetLibrary service

codes.heading: Plucker
codes.notes: A proprietary format for use with Plucker reader software on Palm and other handheld devices [File extension .pdb – see also E114, E121, E125]

codes.heading: VitalBook
codes.notes: A format proprietary to the VitalSource service

codes.heading: Vook
codes.notes: A proprietary digital product combining text and video content and available to be used online or as a downloadable application for a mobile device – see www.vook.com

codes.heading: Google Edition
codes.notes: An epublication made available by Google in association with a publisher; readable online on a browser-enabled device and offline on designated ebook readers

codes.heading: Book ‘app’ for iOS
codes.notes: Epublication packaged as application for iOS (eg Apple iPhone, iPad etc), containing both executable code and content. Use <ProductContentType> to describe content, and <ProductFormFeatureType> to list detailed technical requirements

codes.heading: Book ‘app’ for Android
codes.notes: Epublication packaged as application for Android (eg Android phone or tablet), containing both executable code and content. Use <ProductContentType> to describe content, and <ProductFormFeatureType> to list detailed technical requirements

codes.heading: Book ‘app’ for other operating system
codes.notes: Epublication packaged as application, containing both executable code and content. Use where other ‘app’ codes are not applicable. Technical requirements such as target operating system and/or device should be provided eg in <ProductFormFeatureType>. Content type (text or text plus various ‘enhancements’) may be described with <ProductContentType>

codes.heading: CEB
codes.notes: Founder Apabi’s proprietary basic e-book format

codes.heading: CEBX
codes.notes: Founder Apabi’s proprietary XML e-book format

codes.heading: iBook
codes.notes: Apple’s iBook format (a proprietary extension of EPUB), can only be read on Apple iOS devices

codes.heading: ePIB
codes.notes: Proprietary format based on EPUB used by Barnes and Noble for fixed-format e-books, readable on NOOK devices and Nook reader software

codes.heading: SCORM
codes.notes: Sharable Content Object Reference Model, standard content and packaging format for e-learning objects

codes.heading: EBP
codes.notes: E-book Plus (proprietary Norwegian e-book format)

codes.heading: Page Perfect
codes.notes: Proprietary format based on PDF used by Barnes and Noble for fixed-format e-books, readable on some NOOK devices and Nook reader software

codes.heading: BRF
codes.notes: (Braille-ready file) Electronic Braille file

codes.heading: Erudit
codes.notes: Proprietary XML format for articles, see for example https://www.cairn.info/services-aux-editeurs.php

codes.heading: Amazon Kindle Print Replica
codes.notes: A format proprietary to Amazon for use with its Kindle reading devices or software readers. Essentially a PDF embedded within a KF8 format file

codes.heading: Comic Book Archive
codes.notes: Format for comic books, consisting primarily of sequentially-named PNG or JPEG images in a zip container

codes.heading: eBraille
codes.notes: DAISY / APH Braille file standard based on EPUB (formerly known as eBRF)

codes.heading: Reflowable
codes.notes: Use this and/or code E201 when a particular e-publication type (specified using codes E100 and upwards) is reflowable or has both fixed layout and reflowable sections or variants, to indicate which option is included in this product

codes.heading: Fixed format
codes.notes: Use this and possibly code E200 when a particular e-publication type (specified using codes E100 and upwards) is fixed layout or has both fixed layout and reflowable sections or variants, to indicate which option is included in this product

codes.heading: Readable offline
codes.notes: All e-publication resources are included within the e-publication package

codes.heading: Requires network connection
codes.notes: E-publication requires a network connection to access some resources (eg an enhanced e-book where video clips are not stored within the e-publication package itself, but are delivered via an internet connection)

codes.heading: Content removed
codes.notes: Resources (eg images) present in other editions have been removed from this product, eg due to rights issues

codes.heading: Visible page numbering
codes.notes: (Mostly fixed-format) e-publication contains visible page numbers. Use with List 196 code 19 if numbering has a print-equivalent

codes.heading: No preferred page progression
codes.notes: For e-publications only, pages may be rendered LTR or RTL (see B606 to B609)

codes.heading: Landscape
codes.notes: Use for fixed-format e-books optimized for landscape display. Also include an indication of the optimal screen aspect ratio

codes.heading: Portrait
codes.notes: Use for fixed-format e-books optimized for portrait display. Also include an indication of the optimal screen aspect ratio

codes.heading: Square
codes.notes: Use for fixed-format e-books optimized for a square display

codes.heading: Vertical scrolling
codes.notes: Use for fixed-format e-publications optimized for vertical scrolling display (‘webtoon format’)

(1.25:1) Use for fixed-format e-books optimized for displays with a 5:4 aspect ratio (eg 1280x1024 pixels etc, assuming square pixels). Note that aspect ratio codes are NOT specific to actual screen dimensions or pixel counts, but to the ratios between two dimensions or two pixel counts
(1.33:1) Use for fixed-format e-books optimized for displays with a 4:3 aspect ratio (eg 800x600, 1024x768, 2048x1536 pixels etc)
(1.5:1) Use for fixed-format e-books optimized for displays with a 3:2 aspect ratio (eg 960x640, 3072x2048 pixels etc)
(1.6:1) Use for fixed-format e-books optimized for displays with a 16:10 aspect ratio (eg 1440x900, 2560x1600 pixels etc)
(1.77:1) Use for fixed-format e-books optimized for displays with a 16:9 aspect ratio (eg 1024x576, 1920x1080, 2048x1152 pixels etc)
(2:1) Use for fixed-format e-books optimized for displays with an 18:9 aspect ratio (eg 2160x1080, 2880x1440 pixels etc)
(2.37:1) Use for fixed-format e-books optimized for displays with an 21:9 (or 64:27) aspect ratio (eg 3840x1644 pixels etc)

codes.heading: Laminated

codes.heading: Calendar with write-in space

codes.heading: Calendar without write-in space

codes.heading: One month per page

codes.heading: One week per page

codes.heading: One day per page

codes.heading: SECAM
codes.notes: SD TV standard for video or DVD

codes.heading: HD
codes.notes: Up to 2K resolution (1920 or 2048 pixels wide) eg for Blu-Ray

codes.heading: UHD
codes.notes: Up to 4K resolution (3840 or 4096 pixels wide) eg for Ultra HD Blu-Ray

codes.heading: 3D video
codes.notes: Eg for Blu-ray 3D

codes.heading: Closed captions
codes.notes: Or subtitles, where visibility may be controlled by the viewer. Use <Language> for the language of the captions / subtitles

codes.heading: Open captions
codes.notes: ‘Burnt-in’ or hard captions or subtitles. Use <Language> for the language of the captions / subtitles

codes.heading: Transcript
codes.notes: Full transcript of audio and audiovisual content, supplied as a separate file (not as captions or subtitles) and included within the product. See also List 158, where a transcript is a separate resource

codes.heading: Sign language interpretation
codes.notes: Full signing of audio and audiovisual content included within the product

codes.heading: Textual description of audio
codes.notes: Closed or open captions / subtitles include descriptions of non-dialogue audio (eg background sounds, music, speaker identification) in addition to dialogue. Use in combination with V210 or V211. Use V210, V211 alone for captions / subtitles that include only dialogue. In some markets, textual description of audio is termed ‘subtitles for the deaf and hard of hearing’ (SDH)

codes.heading: Audio description of video
codes.notes: Also termed ‘described video’ – audio track describes the video content as a spoken narration of crucial visual information, usually inserted during pauses in main dialogue

codes.heading: Home use
codes.notes: Licensed for use in domestic contexts only

codes.heading: Classroom use
codes.notes: Licensed for use in education

codes.heading: Wooden
codes.notes: Primary material composition (eg of kit or puzzle pieces, of gameplay tokens or tiles) is wood or has wooden pieces / parts

codes.heading: Plastic
codes.notes: Plastic or plastic pieces / parts

codes.heading: Board
codes.notes: Card or board pieces / parts

codes.heading: 3D puzzle
codes.notes: Puzzle assembles into a 3D object

codes.heading: Noisy kit / puzzle / toy
codes.notes: Toy makes a noise. See B208 for noisy books

codes.heading: Puppet
codes.notes: Including finger / hand puppets, marionettes

codes.heading: Extra large pieces
codes.notes: Designed and sized for the very young, or those with visual impairments, limited motor skills, dementia etc
